[text-1] heading "Install"
[text-2] code "npm init playwright@latest"
[text-3] "Or add manually:"
[text-4] code "npm i -D @playwright/test\nnpx playwright install"
[text-5] heading "Write a test"
[text-6] code "import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';\n\ntest('has title', async ({ page }) => {\n  await page.goto('https://playwright.dev/');\n  await expect(page).toHaveTitle(/Playwright/);\n});\n\ntest('get started link', async ({ page }) => {\n  await page.goto('https://playwright.dev/');\n  await page.getBy"
[text-7] heading "Run tests"
[text-8] code "npx playwright test"
[text-9] "Tests run in parallel across all configured browsers, in headless mode by default. Each test gets a fresh browser context — full isolation with near-zero overhead."
[text-10] heading "Key capabilities"
[text-11] "Auto-wait and web-first assertions. No artificial timeouts. Playwright waits for elements to be actionable, and assertions automatically retry until conditions are met."
[text-12] "Locators. Find elements with resilient locators that mirror how users see the page:"
[text-13] code "page.getByRole('button', { name: 'Submit' })\npage.getByLabel('Email')\npage.getByPlaceholder('Search...')\npage.getByTestId('login-form')"
[text-14] "Test isolation. Each test runs in its own browser context — equivalent to a fresh browser profile. Save authentication state once and reuse it across tests:"
[text-15] code "// Save state after login\nawait page.context().storageState({ path: 'auth.json' });\n\n// Reuse in other tests\ntest.use({ storageState: 'auth.json' });"
[text-16] "Tracing. Capture execution traces, screenshots, and videos on failure. Inspect every action, DOM snapshot, network request, and console message in the Trace Viewer:"
[text-17] code "// playwright.config.ts\nexport default defineConfig({\n  use: {\n    trace: 'on-first-retry',\n  },\n});"
[text-18] code "npx playwright show-trace trace.zip"
[text-19] "Parallelism. Tests run in parallel by default across all configured browsers."
[text-20] "Playwright CLI is a command-line interface for browser automation designed for coding agents. It's more token-efficient than MCP — commands avoid loading large tool schemas and accessibility trees into the model context."
[text-21] code "npm install -g @playwright/cli@latest"
[text-22] "Optionally install skills for richer agent integration:"
[text-23] code "playwright-cli install --skills"
[text-24] heading "Usage"
[text-25] "Point your coding agent at a task:"
[text-26] code "Test the \"add todo\" flow on https://demo.playwright.dev/todomvc using playwright-cli.\nTake screenshots for all successful and failing scenarios."

options.back: go back to the previous page
options.press: press a key: enter, escape, space or an arrow key
options.read: read the page aloud or show its contents
options.clear: clear the text in the focused field
options.stop: stop what the browser is doing
options.none: not a command for this page: a remark, a question, a name, noise
options.play: music: find a song or video by the words and play it now, on YouTube or on this site as the words point — never the page's play button, which is a click
options.play_next: music: find a song by the words and play it after the one playing
options.queue: music: find a song by the words and add it to the end of the queue

slot.instructions: Which words of the transcript are the thing the command carries verbatim: the address to open, the search terms, the song to play, the text to type, the key to press? Never the command word itself: "play X" carries X. Choose none when it carries none.

options.none: the command carries no words of its own

extent.instructions: Only when the action scrolls the page or a scrolling part of it: how far? Choose words when the words give a number of screens or pages; screen when they say nothing of how far. Ignored for every other action.

options.words: as many screens as the number the words carry
options.little: a little: a third of a screen
options.screen: one screen, as Page Down does
options.end: all the way: to the bottom, or to the top going up

where.instructions: Where do the words point: at something on this page, at something on github.com that is not on this page, or somewhere else on the web?

options.page: on this page: one of the numbered refs
options.site: on github.com but not on this page: a page, a person, a post, a section of it
options.web: elsewhere: another website, or a search of the whole web

outcome.instructions: Is what the user asked for done? First: if a pop-up, sign-in prompt, cookie notice or challenge covers the page now, choose in_the_way. Otherwise judge by their words and Done so far, not by the page alone: choose yes when the page shows what they asked to see, or the action they asked for has happened; not_yet when more steps are needed.

options.yes: done: the page shows it, or the action they asked for has happened
options.in_the_way: a pop-up or prompt covers the page now
options.not_yet: not done: more to do, nothing covering the page

progress.instructions: Did the last action in Done so far bring the page closer to what the user's words ask for? Judge by what it did and the page now: closer when it did part or all of what they asked, or opened the way to it; not closer when what changed is not what they asked for.
